clue.text: Dodgy dealings exposed by astute medical centre

parts.note: an astute person is sharp, quick-witted
a doctors' surgery is a medical practice

explanation.surface: A shrewd doctors' surgery is caught out running a crooked scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names dishonest but barely legal business conduct, which is what dodgy dealings are.

clue.text: Magazine proprietors finally left Rugby, say?

parts.note: The Spectator is a long-running British weekly magazine

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word proprietors

parts.note: port is the nautical word for the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: The owners of a magazine at last walk away from a rugby team or school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rugby' looks like the town or school; it is the game, offered as one example ('say?') of a sport people watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby is a game drawing large crowds of onlookers, an example of the category, flagged by 'say?'.

clue.text: For Greeks, a sacred river first of all

parts.note: Alph is the sacred river in Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan

indicators.note: first of signals taking just the opening letter of the word all

explanation.surface: Ancient Greeks are said to have revered a holy river above everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of all' reads as a phrase meaning 'above everything'; split it, so 'first of' picks the initial letter of 'all'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek alphabet's opening letter corresponds to our letter a, so for Greeks a is this letter.

clue.text: Plant protector only Len put out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of only Len put are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A gardener named Len is the only one who set up the cover for the plants.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a long plastic-covered hoop frame used by gardeners to shelter growing crops.

clue.text: Back minister introducing minority language

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a minister
Erse is the Gaelic of Ireland or Scotland, spoken by a minority

explanation.surface: A clergyman supports bringing in a language few people speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a verb of support; it is the noun for the rear side, as in the back of a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The reverse of a coin or page is its back or other side, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Celebrity dips into dictionary — it bears fruit

indicators.note: dips into says the celebrity word goes down inside the dictionary word

parts.note: COD is the Concise Oxford Dictionary
a celebrity is a star

explanation.surface: A famous person browses a dictionary and finds an entry about a fruit-bearing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Costard is an old English apple variety, so the tree of that name produces fruit.

clue.text: Smooth Federalist leaders symbolise it

definitions.meaning: to press creases out of clothes with a hot appliance
the opening letters of Federalist, F and e, form Fe, the chemical symbol of this metal

explanation.surface: Smooth leaders of a federalist party stand for something.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing clothes flat is smoothing them, and the metal element has the symbol Fe.

clue.text: London resident and European, equally soft-hearted

parts.note: as means to the same degree, as in 'as good'
a tender person is soft-hearted

explanation.surface: A Londoner and a fellow European are both kind-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the traditionally working-class area of east London, and the name is also the title of a BBC soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lives in the eastern district of London is a resident of the city.

clue.text: Similarly, they beat monks, somehow touring east

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the shuffled letters go around the compass point
somehow says the letters of they beat monks are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: A violent picture of people beating monks while travelling around the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges THEY BEAT MONKS, and 'touring' wraps those letters round E.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for 'in the same way' or 'likewise', introducing a parallel point.

clue.text: Throw out slippery customer pinching 10p

indicators.note: pinching means grabbing and holding, so the fish's letters close around the money

parts.note: an eel is the classic slippery customer
X is the Roman numeral ten and p stands for pence

explanation.surface: Eject a crook who has stolen ten pence.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject someone from a place or group is to force them out, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Books turned out by peer knowing how sticky liquids flow?

indicators.note: turned out means evicted, so the books are thrown out of the peer's title

parts.note: a viscount is a rank of the British peerage
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books
a knowing look is a sly one

explanation.surface: Books ejected by a crafty nobleman, apparently an expert on syrupy fluids.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing NT from VISCOUNT leaves VISCOU.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick, gooey fluids move slowly and stickily, which is the manner described by this adverb.

clue.text: Desert transport rejected by male supporter of Oxford Movement

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the desert and transport words are read backwards

parts.note: to rat on someone is to desert them
a cart is a means of transport
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: A camel or similar desert carrier is turned down by a man backing a church movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert transport' looks like a camel, but the two words work separately, 'Desert' as a verb meaning abandon; 'rejected' turns them round to give TRACTAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford Movement's founders published 'Tracts for the Times', so their followers took this name from those pamphlets.

clue.text: Jacob's wife? Sounds like Cordelia's father!

indicators.note: sounds like says the word is identified by how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: in Shakespeare, Cordelia is King Lear's youngest daughter

explanation.surface: A quiz question pairing a Bible wife with a Shakespeare father.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the final R is silent, so the king's name and the biblical name are spoken alike.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Jacob married two sisters, and the elder, Rachel's sister, bears this name.

clue.text: Current edible fungus served on board — it's OK

indicators.note: served on puts the food onto the board, so those letters sit above it in this down entry

parts.note: AC is alternating current
the cep is an edible mushroom, the porcini
a board is a table, as in 'board and lodging'

explanation.surface: Mushrooms served on a table with a current running through it are fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something satisfactory or passable is all right, which is what the informal OK means.

clue.text: Slaughter forest keeper ultimately associated with big cat

indicators.note: ultimately points to the closing letters of the words forest and keeper

parts.note: the ounce is another name for the snow leopard

explanation.surface: A gamekeeper ends up in a fatal encounter with a large wild cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slaughter' is used in its sporting sense of a crushing win.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport, to slaughter opponents is to beat them overwhelmingly, the same as thrashing them.

clue.text: Defeat the endless argument supporting deliveries

indicators.note: supporting means holding up from below, so these letters come under the cricket word in this down entry

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled

indicators.note: endless says the word the loses its final letter

parts.note: a row is a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: A cricket argument about bowled balls rumbles on, ending in a loss.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: To topple or bring down a ruler or regime is to defeat them, as in a coup.

clue.text: Rebel leader locked up by some of the French for ages!

indicators.note: locked up by means held inside, so the rebel goes within the French word

parts.note: des is French for 'some of the'
Jack Cade led the Kentish rebellion of 1450

explanation.surface: A rebel chief is imprisoned by the French for a very long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages is the informal for a long time, and many ten-year spans make exactly that.

clue.text: Double-breasted jackets originally exhibited in adverts

indicators.note: in places the picked letter inside the verb for adverts

parts.note: to advert to something is to refer to it

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter of exhibited is used

explanation.surface: Smart jackets first shown in advertisements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adverts' is not advertisements but the verb: to advert to is to refer to.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is a thick double-breasted jacket, originally worn by sailors.

clue.text: Way Austrian physicist keeps old bear

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the old letter sits inside the way and physicist

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
Ernst Mach, after whom the Mach number is named

explanation.surface: An Austrian scientist on his way keeps an elderly bear.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up with or tolerate something unpleasant is to bear it, as in 'I can't stand him'.

clue.text: Proposition boy soldiers misunderstood at first

parts.note: Theo is a boy's name
RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word misunderstood

explanation.surface: A suggestion made by a lad to some troops is initially misread.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a proposition to be proved from axioms is a theorem.

clue.text: Principal girl's initial attention engaged by speedy drivers?

parts.note: top means principal or leading

indicators.note: initial signals the first letter of the word girl's

parts.note: to give someone an ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: The leading lady's first attention is captured by fast drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged' reads as part of the girl's romance; it is gears being engaged in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest ratio in a gearbox is the one a motorist selects when going fast.

clue.text: Place and time to strike on green

parts.note: to place something is to put it down

explanation.surface: Choosing where and when to go on strike on a village green.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, a gentle stroke played on the green towards the hole has this name.

clue.text: Member involved in, say, Ulster disturbance a fellow-countryman

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up within, so the member goes inside the garment

parts.note: an ulster is a long heavy overcoat, an example of a coat
MP is a Member of Parliament
a riot is a violent public disturbance

explanation.surface: An MP caught up in trouble in Northern Ireland is a fellow citizen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ulster' looks like Northern Ireland; here it is a long overcoat, with 'say' marking it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from one's own nation is a fellow citizen, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: One clear about parking being awkward

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: about means around, so the clear word surrounds the parking letter

parts.note: net profit is what you clear after costs
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Someone with no clue about parking is clumsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy, unskilful handling is the sense shared by the two words.

clue.text: Russian woman missing source of river

indicators.note: a river's source is where it begins, so the first letter of the river is lost

parts.note: the Volga is Russia's great river

explanation.surface: A Russian lady has gone missing near the head of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common Russian female first name, as borne by Saint Olga of Kiev.

clue.text: Further issue mostly raised when lacking a hire contract

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the letter a is dropped as well
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the raised word goes

parts.note: to rear children is to raise them
a lease is a contract for hiring property

explanation.surface: Something nearly put up again when there was no rental agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts REARED to REARE; 'lacking' then drops A to leave RERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting out a record or film again is issuing it a second time.

clue.text: Dismal swimmer in river

definitions.meaning: a small silvery freshwater fish of European rivers

explanation.surface: A gloomy picture of a fish swimming in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means cheerless; the noun is a little carp-family fish found in rivers.

clue.text: Battered by elements, survive at end of hike in mountain

parts.note: to weather a storm is to survive it

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the mountain word

parts.note: ben is a Scottish mountain, as in Ben Nevis

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word hike

explanation.surface: Getting through a storm at the end of a mountain trek, battered by the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' with the E ending 'hike' gives ATE, which goes inside BEN after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn and roughened by long exposure to wind and rain is the sense of this compound adjective.
